 LTFRB deploys personnel to PNP border control points for ASEAN Summit
 by 
 Raymond Carl Dela Cruz
 Nov 16, 2026
 5:28 PM GMT+8
 BORDER CONTROL POINT. LTFRB personnel assist the Philippine National Police (PNP) in manning border control points between Quezon City and adjacent provinces for the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in this undated photo. Acting LTFRB chairperson Greg Pua Jr. said the agency's role is limited to assisting in security and traffic enforcement, particularly in intercepting out-of-line and overloaded vehicles entering Metro Manila. (Photo courtesy of LTFRB)
 MANILA – The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) has deployed personnel to assist the Philippine National Police (PNP) in manning border control points between Quezon City and adjacent provinces for the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit.
In a statement on Monday, Acting LTFRB chairperson Greg Pua Jr. said the agency's role is limited to assisting in security and traffic enforcement, particularly in intercepting out-of-line and overloaded vehicles entering Metro Manila.
LTFRB personnel will also guard against colorum public utility vehicles and unsafe public land transportation.
Pua said the agency coordinated with the Quezon City Police District to identify areas needing assistance.
"Our personnel were specifically requested to assist in manning border control points between Quezon City and adjacent provinces," he said.
The deployment was carried out on Nov. 13, initially covering the Barangay Payatas and Batasan-San Mateo border control points.
Quezon City Police District director Brig. Gen. Christopher Olazo requested the deployment in line with President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.'s directive to ensure a safe and orderly hosting of the summit.
"The LTFRB is one with the PNP and all the government agencies in achieving the goal of a peaceful, safe, and successful hosting of the ASEAN Summit," he said.
The agency has also been conducting random and surprise inspections of public utility vehicles to ensure roadworthiness amid the expected increase in passengers for the ASEAN break, which runs from Nov. 15 to 18, 2026.
 He said the LTFRB will maintain a standby force ready for deployment upon the request of the PNP and other agencies. (PNA)
